root_idea.summary: The root develops along two principal orientations: cutting off or coming to an end, and performing a good deed or bestowing a favor.
root_idea.development: The cutting branch yields meanings such as depletion, death, exhaustion, and an unending or undiminished state when negated. The benefaction branch yields granting favor, bestowed provision, and the social extension of reminding or reproaching someone for a gift.

senses.definition: To confer or bestow a favor or benefit upon someone.
senses.usage_conditions: Used for the granting of favor or grace, whether by God or by a human benefactor; the construction may take عَلَيْهِ or بِـ.

senses.definition: To remind someone of a favor, reproach them for it, or count it against them.
senses.usage_conditions: A social and verbal use in which a gift or past action is recounted as leverage or as a claim over the recipient.

senses.definition: To give while seeking a greater return in exchange.
senses.usage_conditions: An interpretation of the construction in 74:6 distinct from verbally reproaching someone for a favor: the giving is performed with the expectation of receiving more.
Used of reward or recompense; the Quranic interpretation includes not being reckoned or limited, not being cut off, and not being reduced.

senses.definition: Death, or the death-dealing vicissitudes of time that diminish life and cut off continuance.
senses.usage_conditions: A Quranic noun used in the expression describing the expectation that the passage or calamities of time will overtake someone.

senses.definition: The manna, a provision bestowed on the Israelites.
senses.usage_conditions: The concrete provision associated in the Quran with the salwā; it is also understood as a bestowed divine blessing.

senses.definition: A favor or benefit, especially when recalled as a reminder or reproach.
senses.usage_conditions: In charitable contexts, the favor may be mentioned in a way that compromises the recipient's dignity or nullifies the merit of the gift.
Used for releasing captives or others without taking a substitute or payment.

other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete measure; this is a Classical lexical use distinct from the Quranic senses of the noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An obligation or burden owed by one person to another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The obligation is associated with a favor received or conferred.
A nominal form of the benefaction branch of the root, distinct in headword from مَنّ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The end or term of time.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in the Classical idiom meaning “until the end of time.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: The main or first rope of a well.

other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensive descriptive form for one who gives abundantly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who gives only while reproaching the recipient and keeping account of the gift.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensive descriptive form for the reproachful social use of giving.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Granted gratuitously or as a favor, rather than as something obligatory.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical or descriptive adjective contrasted with what is obligatory.

cautions: The Lane supplement was matched through geminate contraction and contains homographic مَنْ and مِنْ material; the affected units are retained as ambiguous or non-semantic audit evidence rather than assigned to root منن.
The Quranic construction in 74:6 supports two reported interpretations: verbal reproachful reminding of a favor, and giving while seeking a greater return.
The QAC occurrence for مَنُون in 52:30 is supplied without a Quran Foundation contextual gloss, so its example gloss is left empty.
